## Description

LetÔÇÖs start by adding some content to our website. To do that, we will use HTML tags and some dummy text.

WeÔÇÖll have three main elements inside the body of the HTML: `header`, `main`, and `footer`.

The `header` tag will have a `nav` tag and inside the `nav` tag there will be a `button` to show accessibility modes when clicked. The button should be a direct child of `nav` tag and the buttonÔÇÖs text should be `Accessibility`.

The `main` tag will have two `section` tags inside. Both sections will feature some text and an image inside. The only difference is that the first one will have a first-level `header` and a `paragraph` tag. The second `section` will have a second-level `header` and a `paragraph` tag. The images should have the `source` and `alt` property.

Lastly, `footer` will have a third-level `header` and a link. You can add more than one link and the links donÔÇÖt have to go anywhere.

You can write what you want for any text or use the [Lorem Ipsum](https://loremipsum.io/) text block.

## Objectives

Your page should:

- Add the necessary HTML elements in the body.

## Example

![img](https://ucarecdn.com/63f3f090-2b81-4d17-a5d3-1444cd55a880/)
title: Content

body:
## Description

After clicking the accessibility button, create three new main groups of elements inside the `nav` tag.

The first group is for changing the HTML font size of the HTML. Create a `span` tag with the id `span-text` and the text `Change text size`. Next, create four radio inputs to choose the different font sizes. The IDs of these inputs, respectively, should be `small-text`, `medium-text`, `large-text`, and `larger-text`. You can adjust other properties like name and value and add a `label` for each input.

In the second group, you can modify the colors of the HTML. Begin by creating a `span` element with the ID `span-color` and the text `Change colors`. Then, like in the previous step, generate three radio inputs for various color options. The IDs for these inputs should be `white-theme`, `yellow-theme`, and `blue-theme`, respectively.

The last group will be just a `button` with the id `button-hide-images` and the text `Hide images`.

Finally, once the accessibility button is clicked again, the newly added elements should be removed.

## Objectives

Your page should:

1. Show the new input and button elements for the accessibility modes after clicking the button;
2. Remove the new elements after clicking the button again.

## Example

![img](https://ucarecdn.com/710f0f24-c42a-49b3-876d-92566f102cf6/)
title: Toggle accessibility modes

body:
## Description

After completing the content, we can explore the various accessibility modes. The initial step is to modify the text/font size of the HTML.

Recall the radio inputs from the previous phase; we will now utilize their values. Once the user selects a text-size option, all text elements within the HTML will adjust their font size accordingly.

One approach to achieve this is utilizing CSS classes to apply the required style.

The size values should be:

- For small text, it should be `16px`.
- For medium text, it should be `24px`.
- For large text, it should be `29px`.
- For larger text, it should be `32px`.

## Objectives

Your page should change to the respective font size of the HTML after clicking on the radio inputs.

## Example

![img](https://ucarecdn.com/1479221b-7f4e-47c3-8581-5a71638279bf/)
title: Accessibility mode for font size

body:
## Description

Let's explore another accessibility mode - adjusting the foreground and background colors of the HTML. By selecting one of the radio inputs available in the second stage, the colors of the HTML will change accordingly. A CSS class can be used to implement this feature.

The color values should be:

- For the white theme, it should be `#000` on `#fff`;
- For the yellow theme, it should be `#000` on `#f5d328`;
- For the blue theme, it should be `#fff` on `#002452`.

## Objectives

Your page should change to the respective color of the HTML after clicking on the radio inputs.

## Example

![img](https://ucarecdn.com/96fa67d2-0aee-4dfc-be14-13c4bd89bef3/)
title: Accessibility mode for background color

body:
## Description

One of the accessibility modes available is the option to hide images on the page. Screen readers prioritize alternative text over the image itself, so hiding the images and displaying only the alt text can be useful.

In this stage, after clicking on the `button-hide-images` button from the second stage, you should only show the alt text of the images and not show the images. To easily do that, change the source of the images to `#` so that we will only see the alt text.

The `hide-image` button should act as a toggle, meaning if the user clicks on it again, the page should show the images again. You can reload the page to do that.

## Objectives

Your page should:

1. Hide the images and show the alt text of the images in the HTML after clicking the `hide-images` button;
2. Load the images back after clicking the button the second time.

## Example

![img](https://ucarecdn.com/13191af7-efcb-48b9-aa38-9cd2ec3059f8/)
title: Accessibility mode for the images
